dedupe_keys.name: debrisheightnet rapid hurricane debris volume estimation from post event aerial imagery across five hurricanes

description: This case study estimates the volume of hurricane debris from a single pass of post-event aerial imagery, to support debris removal planning, contracting and federal reimbursement that currently rely on parametric forecasts or on truck-load tallies. The authors published it as a preprint. DebrisHeightNet is a small network head on two frozen vision foundation models, Depth Anything V2 for height and CLIPSeg-debris for segmentation, trained on a target built by confidence-weighted fusion of LiDAR and monocular depth, with a regional power-law calibration to reported hauled volumes. Coverage is ten regions affected by five hurricanes in three US states. The preprint is free to read and download on arXiv. Caveats: the fused training target is a constructed signal, not ground truth, calibration depends on reported hauling records, and the code and data availability are not stated in the abstract read. The authors report that the uncalibrated model agrees with an independent drone survey at a Spearman correlation of 0.87 and lands within 30 percent of the reported record where Hazus and FEMA-hybrid parametric forecasts over-predict by 2.7 to 4.8 times. Simulation uses: rapid post-event analysis of debris quantities for waste management and recovery planning, and calibrating debris generation in hurricane impact models. Related records: the EPA disaster debris recovery tool (data-epa-disaster-debris-recovery-tool) lists debris facilities and the CRS disaster debris report (data-crs-disaster-debris-management-r44941) sets out federal policy.
